summary: Zenno Ishigami was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Taisho University (~1949–1956). He held professorial and emeritus posts at Taisho University (1963–2000), served as president of Shukutoku Junior College (2002–2014), and headed Jodo Shu Research Institute (~2004–2008).

Zennosuke Tsuji was a historian and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1896–1899). He later held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1923–1938), Rissho University (~1946–1955), and the University of the Sacred Heart (~1948–1955).

Zenryu Tsukamoto was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar educated at Bukkyo, Shukyo, and Kyoto universities under teachers including Mochizuki, Yabuki, Shiio, Kuwabara, and Haneda. He served at Kyoto University, as Kyoto National Museum director (1961–1972), and Kacho Junior College president (1973).
Zesho Machida was a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as bettō at Minobusan Okunoin Shishinkaku (attested 1990) and held an emeritus professor post at Minobusan University (attested 1996–2001).
Zhao Luo is a scholar in Buddhist studies, archaeology, and Tibetology who studied under Sen Wang. He held a scholar post at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (attested 2014).
Zhaohua Yang is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He held posts at Stanford University (attested 2007) and Columbia University (attested 2018).

Zhe Ji is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who earned a Ph.D. in sociology at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences in 2007. He was an Associate Professor at INALCO (attested 2011–2017).
Zhen Liu is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned master's degrees from the University of Munich in 2005 and Lanzhou University in 2009.
Zhengyan is a figure in Buddhist and religious studies who studied as a disciple under Yin Shun in 1963. She founded the Tzu Chi Foundation in 1966 and Tzu Chi University in 2000.
Zhenhua was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tianning Buddhist College (1947) and under Yin Shun (1952). He served as manager at the Fuyan Buddhist Institute (attested 1992).

Zhihua Yao specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies, completing a PhD at Boston University (~1997–2002) under Malcolm David Eckel. He held posts at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2004) and the University of Hong Kong (2005).

Zhiru Ng is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She earned an MA at the University of Michigan under Luis Oscar Gómez and a PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello.

Zhiru Shi is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned an MA at the University of Michigan and a PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello. She became an Associate Professor at Pomona College (attested 2007–2014).

Zhiyi Yang is a Sinology scholar who studied at Peking University, Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg, and Princeton University under Martin Kern. She held posts at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg and Goethe University Frankfurt (attested 2015).

Zhonghui Cui is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She completed an MA at SOAS University of London and a PhD at the University of Hong Kong, where she later served as a teaching consultant (attested 2013).
Zhongpei Zhang was a historian and archaeologist who studied under Su Bai (~1952–1956). He later served as director of the Palace Museum (~1987–1991).

Zhongxin Jiang was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji (~1962–1968). He held posts at Peking University (~1968–1978), the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978–2002), and Soka University (~1999).
Zhuan Dao was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Tongzhi. He founded Poo Thor Jee in 1911 and Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery in 1920.
Zijie Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and served as a JSPS research fellow (both attested 2015).

Zoltán Gombocz was a scholar in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his secondary education at the Berzsenyi Dániel Lyceum in 1895 and studied at Eötvös Loránd University from 1895 to 1900.
